transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-22
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM) -- Celestia: Carlos (CTO), Leah (PM), Marc (SRE), Aisha (Security)

Summary:
QBR style health check focusing on usage trends (noted spike in embeddings), cost optimization, recent reliability blips, and roadmap alignment for Dedicated / Private options. Customer concerned about rising token costs and two 15-min outages in August; exploring Dedicated capacity to stabilize latency and predictable unit economics. Security asks: SOC2 docs, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs retention. Next steps agreed: Redwood to send dashboards, propose Dedicated pilot, share security pack, and schedule Redwood Optimize demo.

Topics discussed:
- Usage & cost trends (Q2->Q3 spike, embeddings use)
- Reliability incidents and root cause / mitigations
- Options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC)
- Roadmap: feature requests around traceability & routing policies
- Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, RBAC, audit retention
- Pilot plan & timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok thanks everyone for joining on time, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, AE, with Sofia who is our solutions engineer and Priya from customer success, um we'll run about 40 minutes, goal is quick QBR and action plan, sound good?
[00:14] Carlos: yep thanks, want to make sure we cover the outages and talk about cost, Leah will jump in on product priorities as well
[00:25] Sofia: great, i'll start with a high level on usage -- so we've seen Celestia's token usage up roughly 3x since May, biggest driver is embeddings calls for the semantic search product, and we also noticed a shift to longer sequence lengths in the chat flow which is pushing costs higher
[00:42] Marc: yeah the embedding batch jobs were increased in August for a migration, that caused a spike, we should also note we hit a couple of throttles on the hosted tier which correlated with the 09/03 and 08/19 incidents
[01:05] Jordan: right, about the reliability blips, do you have the incident notes Marc or should we summarize what we saw on our end?
[01:12] Marc: i can do quick-- so on 08/19 we had a 15 minute period where requests to the endpoint were queuing, p95 latency doubled, our app fallback kicked in; the root cause was a combination of a model variant falling back to a slower CPU variant plus sustained embedding throughput, so KV cache wasn't warming as expected
[01:36] Sofia: yep and on Redwood's side we saw a transient autoscaler delay for very bursty traffic and a fallback to a smaller model variant, that's what caused the increased latency. we've since adjusted the autoscaling thresholds and improved the model routing heuristics, but for predictable latency we recommended Dedicated capacity
[02:00] Leah: can you explain the Dedicated vs Hosted economics? we want predictable performance but not sure on cost delta or commit sizes
[02:09] Jordan: sure -- Hosted is pay-as-you-go, great for bursty dev traffic; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and a much lower per-token unit cost once you cross certain usage. for your current footprint we estimate a 20-35% cost reduction on generation tokens, embeddings even more depending on batching and quantization choices
[02:33] Leah: 20-35% is interesting, does that include savings from batching/kv cache?
[02:38] Sofia: that's factoring in optimized batching, prefix/KV cache hit improvements, and ability to pin a quantized variant. Redwood Optimize can propose quantization and batching profiles based on your traffic -- we can run a quick analysis with sample traces
[02:54] Aisha: on security side we need SOC2 and encryption details, specifically KMS integration and key rotation. also how are audit logs retained in Dedicated vs Private?
03:03 Marc (transcription glitch as 'Mark'): um i can add to that, we need tenant-level audit trails and the ability to forward logs to our SIEM
[03:12] Priya: ok noted, Aisha -- we will share the SOC2 pack and KMS integration guide. Dedicated gives you audit logs with configurable retention and can be forwarded to your logging endpoint; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives full network control if you need air-gapped option
[03:29] Carlos: timeline wise, if we wanted to pilot Dedicated what does that look like? we have a org-wide migration planned for Q4 so would like to decide by mid-october
[03:40] Sofia: typical path is a 2-week pilot with dedicated pool sizing based on your p95 throughput and seq length distribution; we can provision a small pool, run benchmark tests (latency, throughput) and a cost delta analysis. Jordan will propose sizing and cost by 9/29
[03:58] Jordan: yep i'll own that. also we'll include an A/B of model variants so you can see quality impact vs cost. any concerns about model compatibility or tool calling?
[04:12] Leah: not yet, product wants better routing controls though -- e.g., route latency-sensitive calls to the low-latency pool and cheaper reranking to a lower-cost variant, can Redwood support that?
[04:24] Sofia: absolutely, we have smart routing policies and per-route model pins in Redwood Console; it's possible to set policy by route and failover to a cheaper region if capacity is constrained. small note — sometimes the console names are transcribed weirdly in notes, like 'Redwood Con-sole' in older downloads
[04:42] Marc: for the August incidents did you capture traces? we want to correlate our app logs with your tracing
[04:49] Priya: yes we captured traces and will share them; we also have a trace hook that can attach request IDs to your logs for easier correlation
[05:02] Aisha: another question on data residency, Celestia's policy requires EU-only storage for embeddings from EU users, can we configure region routing per-tenant?
[05:13] Sofia: yes, region routing is supported; you can pin routes to EU regions and we can enforce data residency. for stricter requirements the Private deployment gives you full control over data at rest and network boundaries
[05:28] Jordan: circling back to costs, one thing that significantly reduces cost is increasing batch windows for offline embedding jobs and enabling int8 quantization where model quality tolerates it. Redwood Optimize can generate candidate quant configs and estimate quality impact using your eval set
[05:45] Leah: what's the SLA for Dedicated? we need p99 targets for certain endpoints
[05:50] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets, we can include p99 latency SLOs for pin-pointed routes in the enterprise addendum. we'll share the SLA draft with pricing
[06:05] Carlos: perfect. any blockers for the pilot? security sign-off looks like the main gating item for us
[06:12] Aisha: yes SOC2 plus our internal IP allowlist and KMS rotation policy. also want to confirm role based access (RBAC) mapping to our SSO groups
[06:22] Priya: we'll include SSO/SAML mapping docs and a sample RBAC mapping; for KMS we support bringing-your-own-keys and HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated via KMS plugins
[06:35] Marc: quick note on observability: can we get token-level cost breakdowns per route? that was really helpful in prior reports
[06:43] Jordan: yes token-level breakdown and per-route dashboards are available in Redwood Console, we'll attach a sample dashboard and export of your past 90 days usage
[06:54] Leah: client asks for a short tech deep-dive for infra team, maybe an hour for SREs next week? could be demo of autoscaling and KV cache behaviour
[07:05] Sofia: sure we can do an SE-led deep dive; i'll propose Wed or Thu next week and include Marc and your infra folks
[07:15] Jordan: ok to recap next steps: Jordan sends usage dashboard and cost breakdown by 9/24, Sofia to propose Dedicated pilot sizing and cost by 9/29, Priya to send SOC2 and KMS docs by 9/25, schedule SE deep-dive for infra next week. Any edits?
[07:33] Carlos: that matches our notes, thanks everyone
[07:37] Leah: thanks all, talk soon
[07:40] Jordan: thanks team, end call

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker labels were noisy (Marc tagged as 'Mark' in a chunk), occasional ASR errors for product names (eg Redwood Optimize transcribed as 'Redwood Opti') and technical terms (KV cache -> KV cash).
